matches.rationale: Both identify an inconsistency between Section 5 (which states BookCorpus is an exception with a non-zero barrier) and Table 2 (which reports 0.00 ± 0.00 for learned matching on BookCorpus). The underlying issue is a data integrity problem: narrative and table contradict each other.

The ground truth describes Equation 2 incorrectly using an infimum instead of a supremum, making the multi-model barrier trivially non-positive. Finding 1 explicitly reports that Eq. (2) uses an infimum, causing the barrier expression to be ≤ 0 and failing to measure worst-case deviation.

Ground truth says the Abstract overclaims universal Transformer alignment without mentioning RoPE limitations; finding 10 states the abstract claims applicability to all Transformer architectures and positional encodings while Appendix F admits RoPE breaks the symmetry group. Both capture the same overgeneralization from limited evidence.

Ground truth points out Algorithm 1 lists an Adam optimizer with unspecified learning rate η, preventing reproduction. No finding observes this missing hyperparameter disclosure; other finding about incomplete specification (pred_id 14) concerns an undefined operator, not a missing learning rate.

Ground truth flags a fabricated citation 'Zhou et al., 2024' for layer-wise linearity, missing from the references. Finding 15 identifies a different missing reference 'Wang and Chen [2024]' for a Transformer result; they are distinct fabricated/missing citations supporting different claims.

Ground truth concerns promotional, exaggerated language in the Introduction that overstates the work (e.g., 'completely solves'). Finding 8 reports the Introduction claims 'achieves perfect zero-barrier connectivity in all cases' and 'definitively proves' universal connectivity, which far exceeds the actual scope and later limitations.

Ground truth says Equation 3 was corrupted to argmin, inverting the alignment objective. Finding 2 states that Eq. (3) uses argmin for positive inner products, anti-aligning weights instead of aligning them—exactly the same logical error.

Ground truth describes removal of a nuanced discussion about BookCorpus higher barriers and possible explanations (selective editing). None of the findings mention a missing discussion paragraph; they note data inconsistencies (pred_id 6) or weight-matching overclaims (pred_id 7), not the absence of this qualitative analysis.

Ground truth notes the diamond operator (◊) in the Figure 2 caption is never defined. Finding 14 states the Figure 2 transformation relies on an undefined 'diamond' operator and the paper defers its definition to the code repository, rendering the method incompletely specified.

Ground truth reports Section 6 corruptly claims weight matching achieves 'perfect alignment,' contradicting the actual Figure 5 showing nearly arbitrary rotations. Finding 7 identifies that Section 6 claims weight matching yields 'perfect alignment' and 'sufficient for zero barriers,' which contradicts the substantial non-zero barriers in Table 2.

Both concern asymmetric use of post-hoc temperature scaling for Tiny ImageNet: the ground truth says it was applied only to the proposed method, and finding 12 explicitly states temperature scaling was applied 'only to our learned matching method' while baselines used uncalibrated logits, yielding an unfair comparison.

Ground truth says the Limitations appendix (Appendix A) was removed, omitting critical context. No finding notes that a limitations section is missing or that important caveats were deleted; findings about overclaiming (8) reference other sections but do not flag removal of Appendix A.

Ground truth argues Figure 4 misrepresentation: the text claims 'near-zero deviation,' but the figure shows substantial positive deviations when interpreted correctly. None of the findings mention Figure 4 or the 'region of near-zero deviation' claim, so this specific visual misrepresentation is not captured.

Ground truth targets misattribution of the Git Re-Basin framework to Singh and Jaggi (2020) instead of Ainsworth et al. (2022). Finding 16 states the text says 'Git Re-Basin framework, first proposed by Singh and Jaggi [2020],' which is a misleading misattribution since Singh and Jaggi introduced OT fusion, not Git Re-Basin.

Ground truth says the Conclusion was corrupted to claim permutations are sufficient, contradicting the Introduction's argument that broader symmetries are needed. Finding 9 reports the Conclusion states 'permutation symmetries alone are sufficient' and then says 'broader symmetry classes are essential,' an internal contradiction that aligns with the cross-section incoherence.
